rationale: To maximize the robot's line-following performance on the held-back track, I designed a balanced geometry with 5 sensors spread evenly across the front to detect the tape line effectively. I chose a moderate sensor size of 0.012 m to balance resolution and coverage. The wheel track and body width are set to 0.14 m to provide stability without excessive width that could cause off-track penalties. The wheel radius is 0.035 m for a good balance of speed and torque, and the mass is set to 1.0 kg for stability and inertia. The controller uses a base speed of 1.5 to ensure a fast pace while maintaining control. PID gains are tuned to moderate values (kp=8, ki=0.5, kd=3) to provide responsive but stable steering. Sensor weights are set to emphasize the center sensors positively and the outer sensors negatively, encouraging the robot to steer back to the line when it drifts. The line loss strategy is set to 'last_direction' to allow the robot to continue searching in the last known direction of the line, reducing stalls. I request measurements including completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation to evaluate both speed and stability. This design aims to achieve high completion rates with minimal line loss and smooth steering, improving overall score.
